new_assertions.title: quotient endpoints plus permutation sign still do not determine phase
new_assertions.body: For the shortest 5x4 routes, the tuple (source quotient 197000, target quotient 197002, accumulated sign 1) occurs with phase 0 and phase 1; phase is not a function of that tuple.

new_assertions.title: current endpoint quotient erases both fine residual and route-orientation distinctions
new_assertions.body: On the shortest 5x4 obstruction, the current quotient identifies fine residual-distinct endpoint states while the same quotient endpoint pair is traversed with distinct full transporters and distinct oriented action histories.

new_assertions.title: target quotient cannot reconstruct distinguished exact residual bit
new_assertions.body: No single-valued function of target quotient node 197002 alone can reproduce the P0 membership bit for residual token 197700 on both represented final states 197402 and 197403.

new_assertions.title: source quotient cannot reconstruct distinguished exact residual bits
new_assertions.body: No single-valued function of source quotient node 197000 alone can reproduce the represented P0 membership pattern of residual tokens 197700 and 197701 on both source sheets.

new_assertions.title: scalar Boolean consistency is not forced by XOR syntax alone
new_assertions.body: The represented Boolean XOR relation admits the concrete 4x4 reconvergence constraint system while the concrete 5x4 obstruction constraint system is inconsistent; scalar consistency depends on the represented incidence/delta constraints rather than following from XOR syntax alone.
new_assertions.scope: comparison of the two concrete primitive-supported witness systems only

new_assertions.title: binary-tie XOR law does not imply continuation-phase integrability
new_assertions.body: The exact binary-tie relation BINARY_TIE_ALLOWED iff XOR-zero and the exact 5x4 scalar-continuation obstruction coexist in the represented system; therefore binary-tie XOR exactness alone does not imply scalar continuation-phase integrability.
new_assertions.scope: represented binary-tie layer versus represented 5x4 continuation layer

new_assertions.title: residual incidence supplies an intrinsic discriminator absent from the current quotient on the witness
new_assertions.body: There exists represented residual-membership structure that distinguishes fine members of both the source and target quotient nodes in the shortest 5x4 obstruction.
new_assertions.note: This asserts discriminator existence only, not sufficiency to repair all syndromes.

new_assertions.title: endpoint quotient is insufficient to reconstruct observed transition orientation/history
new_assertions.body: The current ordered quotient endpoint pair is insufficient to reconstruct either the observed accumulated full-transporter identity or the observed source-frame action-sequence identity on the shortest 5x4 routes.

support_refinements.witness: Two route observations have the same sign bit and different phase bits.
support_refinements.note: Adds primitive cross-incidence support to the source-explicit permutation-sign falsifier.

rejected_candidates.body: Because residual incidence distinguishes the shortest witness, residual incidence is the minimal corrected phase coordinate.
rejected_candidates.reason: Discrimination is necessary evidence but does not establish minimality or global sufficiency.

rejected_candidates.body: The 4x4 constant assignment proves all width-4 carriers are integrable.
rejected_candidates.reason: The assertion widens one concrete witness to an unrepresented family theorem; width-4 generalization remains QU-SC-002.
